reviewer: mc3_packet_probe, independent wheel helper author review requested by mc3_texture_probe
resolution: accept the qualified source-derived static scale composition; no runtime fidelity approval

source_chain_review.car: Config indices write width table values to +12d4(front)/+12cc(rear), profile selectors to +11b8/+11bc and diameter/profile ratios to +12d8/+12d0. FUN002f85d0 writes (2width,ratio,ratio) into axle basis state. FUN003042c8 loads the wheel frame, copies radial columns into the tire draw matrix, then multiplies the rim radial columns by FUN002ca758 which returns profile table value. Thus rim radial scale is ratio*profile; tire radial scale remains ratio.
source_chain_review.bike: FUN002f6c48 reads pose-frame Y at +0x28, doubles it into both radial scale state locations; FUN002f85d0 selects that state and forces X basis to1. FUN003042c8 reads the own wheel joint auxiliary pointer at joint+0x40, selects transmaxX at auxiliary+0x24, multiplies by4 and constructor +0x11d8 float(.89), and scales rim/tire X before copying the tire matrix. It then multiplies only the rim radial columns by constructor +0x11d0(.7) or+0x11d4(.85), selected by classenum5 in FUN004b2220.
source_chain_review.component_identity: Native assembly assigns rim handle to +0xcc and front/rear tire handles to +0xc4/+0xc8. Rim drawing uses fStack3c0; tire drawing uses fStack300, which was copied before the rim-specific factor.

claim_limits: This independently resolves the semantic scale chain under a source rest-pose assumption. Native animation, camber, suspension, tire deformation and runtime exact float rounding remain outside this audit.
Auxiliary transmaxX is a DoF constraint source value consumed as width by the native bike renderer, not a generic geometry bbox.
The numerical 94-vehicle/346-joint comparison is recorded separately in wheel-scale-independent-composition.json.
